name: veyq
//: Repo-root manifest for ONE reason: the pnpm workspace (`pnpm-workspace.yaml` lists its members), so `src/web/` and `src/admin-web/` resolve the same `@veyq/crypto` on disk instead of each carrying a copy (ADR 0065 — duplicating the crypto suite would be a security defect, not a maintenance nuisance). It is deliberately not a build orchestrator: each surface keeps its own `pnpm run check` and is proven on its own, and nothing here aggregates them. Adding a workspace member is the whole feature set. The overrides and the dependency build-script decisions, with why each stands, live in `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, where pnpm reads them.
//engines: The Node the workspace supports, stated so a wrong local one is named once, here, instead of as one EBADENGINE warning per package (inbox #353). It is the intersection of what the locked tree declares (measured 2026-10-10: abbrev and nopt `^22.22.2 || ^24.15.0 || >=26.0.0`, the eslint family `^20.19.0 || ^22.13.0 || >=24`, vitest `^20.0.0 || ^22.0.0 || >=24.0.0`). The images and CI run Node 22 (the Dockerfiles' `node:22-bookworm-slim`, the workflows' `node-version: "22"`); an odd, non-LTS release such as 23 is outside every one of those ranges.
//packageManager: pnpm, exactly: one content-addressed store shared by every checkout instead of a ~470 MB node_modules each, and a strict node_modules that links a member only what it declares. A pnpm of another version run here switches itself to the pinned one (measured 2026-11-03: pnpm 12.16.1 in a package pinning 12.15.0 ran 12.15.0), and pnpm-lock.yaml's first document pins pnpm's own executables by integrity. Every place a build installs pnpm (`npm install -g pnpm@<x.y.z>` in the workflows and Dockerfiles) names this version, and site/package.json pins the same — scripts/validate_pnpm_installs_gated.py holds them equal. Bumping it: change every one in one commit, then `pnpm install` here and in site/ so each lockfile's first document follows.
//lockfile: Bumping by hand (no remote, so no Dependabot): raise the floor in the member's package.json to the fixed version, then `pnpm install` (it re-resolves what changed and keeps the rest), or `pnpm update -r <package>`. A package shared by src/web/ and src/admin-web/ must stay ONE version: two Vue runtimes in one bundle is the defect (it bit under npm, inbox #403, when both members' ranges moved past the hoisted copy). `pnpm why -r <package>` names the versions in the tree, and `pnpm dedupe --check` is red when the lockfile could carry fewer copies. Install through `python3 scripts/pnpm_install_no_deprecated.py` before committing a lockfile change: it is the deprecation gate CI runs.
